listings.title: Chat and writing
listings.summary: Answer questions, draft and edit text, and summarise documents with a model that runs on your graphics card.
listings.description: Installs Ollama if it is missing, then one chat model sized for this PC. Every AI window can pick it afterwards. The Store picks the largest variant that fits; you can choose another before installing.

variants.title: GPT-OSS 120B
variants.summary: OpenAI's larger open-weight model, for machines with a lot of graphics memory.

variants.title: Qwen3.5 27B
variants.summary: Dense 27B model for writing and longer tasks.

variants.title: GPT-OSS 20B
variants.summary: Reads 3.6B of its 21B parameters per token, so it answers quickly for its size.

variants.title: Qwen3.5 9B
variants.summary: General chat on a mid-range graphics card.

variants.title: Qwen3.5 4B
variants.summary: For smaller or older graphics cards.

listings.title: Fast helper
listings.summary: A small model for the quick jobs behind every message: routing, search queries and conversation titles.
listings.description: The router, title and search roles run on every message, so they want a model that answers in well under a second. Assign it in Preferences → Models after installing.

listings.title: Sees images
listings.summary: Describe pictures and screenshots, read the text in them and answer questions about them.
listings.description: A model that takes images as input. It backs image captions in the Library and any AI window you attach a picture to.

listings.title: Coding agent
listings.summary: Drive the Code window's built-in agent with a local model that edits files through tool calls.
listings.description: The native harness reads the workspace, runs commands through the danger guard and proposes edits. Local models become dependable at this from about 14B parameters.

listings.title: Qwen3 0.6B
listings.summary: The smallest Qwen3 model. Enough for routing and titles, not for long answers.

listings.title: Gemma 3 1B
listings.summary: Google's smallest Gemma 3 model, text only.

listings.title: Llama 3.2 3B
listings.summary: Meta's small Llama 3.2 model for short chats and helper jobs.

listings.title: Qwen3 4B
listings.summary: Small Qwen3 model for helper jobs and short chats. It can think before answering.

listings.title: Gemma 3 4B
listings.summary: Small Gemma 3 model that reads images as well as text.

listings.title: Llama 3.1 8B
listings.summary: Meta's 8B Llama 3.1 model for general chat.

listings.title: Qwen3 8B
listings.summary: 8B Qwen3 model for general chat. It can think before answering.

listings.title: DeepSeek R1 8B
listings.summary: DeepSeek R1 distilled into Qwen3 8B. It writes out its reasoning before the answer, so replies take longer.

listings.title: Gemma 3 12B
listings.summary: Mid-size Gemma 3 model for writing and questions about images.

listings.title: Mistral Small 3.2 24B
listings.summary: Mistral's 24B model with tool calls and image input.

listings.title: Gemma 3 27B
listings.summary: The largest Gemma 3 model, for writing and describing images.

listings.title: GPT-OSS 20B
listings.summary: OpenAI's open-weight mixture-of-experts model: 21B parameters, 3.6B of them active per token.

listings.title: GPT-OSS 120B
listings.summary: OpenAI's larger open-weight model: 117B parameters, 5.1B of them active per token.

listings.title: Qwen3 32B
listings.summary: The largest dense Qwen3 model. It can think before answering.

listings.title: Qwen2.5-VL 7B
listings.summary: Qwen vision model for screenshots, documents and photos.

listings.title: Llama 3.2 Vision 11B
listings.summary: Meta's Llama 3.2 model with image input.

listings.title: Qwen2.5 Coder 3B
listings.summary: Small code model for completions and short edits.

listings.title: Qwen2.5 Coder 7B
listings.summary: Code model for completions, edits and light agent work.

listings.title: Qwen2.5 Coder 14B
listings.summary: Code model sized for multi-step edits with tool calls.

listings.title: Devstral 24B
listings.summary: Mistral's code model trained for agents that edit repositories with tools.
listings.description: Architecture numbers come from Devstral Small 2507; Ollama's devstral:24b has the same parameter count and layout.

listings.title: Qwen3 Coder 30B-A3B
listings.summary: Qwen's mixture-of-experts code model: 30.5B parameters, 3.3B of them active per token.

listings.title: Qwen3.5 4B
listings.summary: Small Qwen3.5 model. Three in four of its layers use linear attention, which keeps long conversations light on memory.

listings.title: Qwen3.5 9B
listings.summary: Qwen3.5 model for general chat on a mid-range graphics card.

listings.title: Qwen3.5 27B
listings.summary: Dense 27B Qwen3.5 model for writing and longer tasks.

listings.title: Qwen3.5 35B-A3B
listings.summary: Qwen3.5 mixture-of-experts model: 35B parameters, 3B of them active per token.

listings.title: Qwen3-VL 8B
listings.summary: Qwen3 vision model that reasons about an image before it answers.

listings.title: Qwen3-VL 30B-A3B
listings.summary: Qwen3 mixture-of-experts vision model for images, screenshots and documents.

listings.title: Devstral Small 2 24B
listings.summary: Mistral's second Devstral Small, a 24B model for coding agents.

listings.title: Make images
listings.summary: Turn a sentence into a picture on your graphics card.
listings.description: Installs the model files for one image lane. ComfyUI must be installed and opened once first. The lane appears on the Visual Canvas and in the comfyui_run tool.

variants.title: Z-Image Turbo
variants.summary: Distilled model that needs few sampling steps.

variants.title: FLUX.1 schnell
variants.summary: Four sampling steps, at full precision.

variants.title: Wan 2.2 5B
variants.summary: One frame from the Wan video model; shares its files with the video lanes.

variants.title: Stable Diffusion XL
variants.summary: 1024-pixel images, with the largest set of community LoRAs.

listings.title: Edit photos
listings.summary: Change a photo by describing the change, such as a new sky or a removed object.
listings.description: The output keeps the size of the source photo. ComfyUI must be installed and opened once first.

listings.title: Make video
listings.summary: Make a short clip from a sentence, or animate a still picture.
listings.description: Both variants use the same three Wan 2.2 5B files, so installing one gives you the other. Clips are about two seconds at 24 frames per second.

listings.title: Upscale
listings.summary: Enlarge an image to four times its width and height.

listings.title: Z-Image Turbo
listings.summary: Text to image with Alibaba's distilled Z-Image Turbo model.
listings.description: Built into Umbrelis; installing it fetches the diffusion model, its Qwen3 4B text encoder and the VAE. The 8 GB minimum is the figure Umbrelis's model catalog records for this model.

listings.title: Qwen-Image Edit 2511
listings.summary: Edit a photo from a written instruction.
listings.description: Built into Umbrelis. The fp8 edit model needs about 16 GB of graphics memory; ComfyUI moves parts to system memory on smaller cards, which is slower.

listings.title: FLUX.1 schnell
listings.summary: Text to image in four sampling steps with Black Forest Labs' schnell model.
listings.description: Built into Umbrelis. The full-precision 12B model needs about 24 GB of graphics memory; ComfyUI moves parts to system memory on smaller cards, which is slower.

listings.title: Stable Diffusion XL
listings.summary: Text to image at 1024 pixels with SDXL base 1.0.
listings.description: Built into Umbrelis. One checkpoint file holds the model, its text encoders and the VAE.

listings.title: SDXL with ControlNet Union
listings.summary: Make an image that follows the edges, depth map or pose in a control image you provide.
listings.description: Built into Umbrelis. The control image must already be an edge map, depth map or pose skeleton; the lane does not extract one from a photo.

listings.title: Upscale 4x (Real-ESRGAN)
listings.summary: Enlarge an image four times with Real-ESRGAN x4plus. No prompt.

listings.title: Wan 2.2 text to image
listings.summary: A single frame from the Wan 2.2 5B video model, used as a still image.
listings.description: Built into Umbrelis. Uses the same files as the Wan 2.2 video lanes. The 5B model runs in 6 to 8 GB of graphics memory.

listings.title: Wan 2.2 image to video
listings.summary: Animate a still picture into a short clip with Wan 2.2 5B.
listings.description: Built into Umbrelis. Saves an mp4. The 5B model runs in 6 to 8 GB of graphics memory at 480p.

listings.title: Wan 2.2 text to video
listings.summary: A clip of about two seconds from a sentence, with Wan 2.2 5B.
listings.description: Built into Umbrelis. Saves an mp4 at 24 frames per second. The 5B model runs in 6 to 8 GB of graphics memory at 480p.

listings.title: Z-Image Turbo diffusion model (bf16)
listings.summary: The Z-Image Turbo diffusion model, repackaged for ComfyUI.

listings.title: Qwen3 4B text encoder
listings.summary: The text encoder Z-Image Turbo reads prompts with.

listings.title: FLUX autoencoder (ae)
listings.summary: The VAE shared by Z-Image Turbo and FLUX.1 schnell.

listings.title: Qwen-Image Edit 2511 diffusion model (fp8)
listings.summary: The Qwen-Image Edit 2511 model in mixed fp8, repackaged for ComfyUI.

listings.title: Qwen2.5-VL 7B text encoder (fp8)
listings.summary: The vision-language encoder Qwen-Image reads prompts and source photos with.

listings.title: Qwen-Image VAE
listings.summary: The autoencoder Qwen-Image models decode pictures with.

listings.title: FLUX.1 schnell diffusion model
listings.summary: Black Forest Labs' FLUX.1 schnell at full precision, repackaged for ComfyUI.

listings.title: CLIP-L text encoder
listings.summary: One of the two text encoders FLUX reads prompts with.

listings.title: T5-XXL text encoder (fp8)
listings.summary: The larger of the two text encoders FLUX reads prompts with, in fp8.
listings.description: The link comes from ComfyUI-Manager's model list; the official ComfyUI templates only reference the scaled and fp16 versions of this encoder.

listings.title: Stable Diffusion XL base 1.0
listings.summary: Stability AI's SDXL base checkpoint: model, text encoders and VAE in one file.

listings.title: ControlNet Union SDXL 1.0
listings.summary: One SDXL ControlNet for edges, depth, pose and scribbles, saved under the name Umbrelis's lane loads.
listings.description: Downloads xinsir's diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors (the standard model, not ProMax) and saves it as controlnet-union-sdxl-1.0.safetensors.

listings.summary: A 4x image upscaling model, 64 MB.
listings.description: The original GitHub release publishes no digest, so the file comes from the lllyasviel/Annotators copy on Hugging Face, which has the same size as the release asset and a published SHA-256.

listings.title: Wan 2.2 TI2V 5B diffusion model (fp16)
listings.summary: Wan 2.2's 5B model for text to video and image to video, repackaged for ComfyUI.

listings.title: Wan 2.2 VAE
listings.summary: The autoencoder for Wan 2.2 5B. The 14B Wan models need the Wan 2.1 VAE instead.

listings.title: UMT5-XXL text encoder (fp8, scaled)
listings.summary: The text encoder Wan models read prompts with.

listings.title: Read text aloud
listings.summary: Speak replies, narration and documents in a voice that is generated on this PC.
listings.description: Kokoro is small and fast with a fixed set of voices; Chatterbox sounds more natural and can copy a voice from a short recording. The assistant's voice and the Studio's narration use whichever you pick in Preferences → Assistant.

variants.title: Chatterbox
variants.summary: About 3.2 GB; copies a voice from five seconds of audio.

listings.description: Runs faster-whisper. Its weights download into the models folder the first time it transcribes, at the size chosen in Preferences → Assistant.

listings.description: Runs Demucs htdemucs. Each stem lands in the Library as its own file.

listings.summary: Speak any text in a voice copied from a recording of five seconds or more.
listings.description: Runs Chatterbox from Resemble AI, which adds an inaudible watermark to what it generates.

listings.title: Clean up a recording
listings.summary: Remove noise from speech, or restore the high frequencies a low-quality recording lost.

variants.title: Speech (Resemble Enhance)
variants.summary: Denoises speech and returns it at 44.1 kHz.

variants.title: Any audio (AudioSR)
variants.summary: Upsamples speech, music or effects to 48 kHz.

listings.title: Kokoro 82M
listings.summary: Small text-to-speech model with fixed voices. Comes with the af_heart voice; other voices install separately.

listings.title: Chatterbox
listings.summary: Text-to-speech from Resemble AI that can copy a voice from a short reference clip.
listings.description: Installs the five files Chatterbox loads: the voice encoder, the T3 and S3Gen models, the tokenizer and the built-in voice.

listings.summary: Denoises speech and extends its bandwidth to 44.1 kHz. Installs its Python packages on first run.

listings.title: AudioSR
listings.summary: Upsamples any audio to 48 kHz by generating the missing high frequencies. Installs about 3 GB of Python packages on first run.

listings.title: Lane prompt writer
listings.summary: Turns a short idea into the full prompt an image, photo-edit or video lane wants, and can put it on the canvas.
listings.description: Follows the same guides as the canvas's built-in writer. Pick a model without a thinking mode: a model that reasons at length before writing tends to run out of room before the prompt.

payload.name: Lane prompt writer
payload.instruction:
You write prompts for lanes on the Umbrelis Visual Canvas. The user gives you a short idea and tells you, or you can read from the canvas, whether it is for an image lane, a photo-edit lane or a video lane. Reply with the finished prompt and nothing else, unless the user asked a question.

Image lane: one paragraph of 60 to 120 words. Name the subject first and describe it concretely (age, clothing, material, expression, pose). Then the setting and what surrounds the subject. Then composition and framing: where the subject sits in the frame, lens feel, depth of field. Then the light (source, direction, quality, time of day) and the palette. End with the medium or style in a few words (photograph, oil painting, flat illustration, 3D render).

Photo-edit lane: one to three imperative sentences. Say exactly what changes (the object, its new look, position or colour), then what must stay the same (the person's identity, the background, the framing, the lighting) so the model edits instead of repainting. One edit per instruction.

Video lane: one paragraph of 90 to 160 words in present tense. Who or what is in frame and how they look; where and at what time of day; what happens, as one continuous action or two beats at most; how the camera moves and the framing; the light and palette. If the lane makes sound, end with one sentence on the soundscape: ambience first, then any spoken line in quotes, then music only if the idea asks for it.

For every lane: stay faithful to the idea and to any reference picture; never add readable text, signs, logos or watermarks unless asked; use specific nouns instead of words like "masterpiece" or "8k"; no negative lists, bullet points, headings or quotes around the whole prompt.

When the user asks you to put the prompt on the canvas: call workspace_state with target "canvas" to find the board and the lane's node id and control keys, then canvas_edit with action "set_values", the lane_node_id, values holding the prompt under the lane's prompt key, and writer "none" so your words reach the model as written. Only run the lane (canvas_edit action "run") when the user asks.

listings.title: Studio editor
listings.summary: Cuts generated clips, songs and voice-overs into a Studio timeline, mixes it, exports it and checks the result.
listings.description: Needs a model that calls tools. A model that sees images can also read the contact sheet media_check returns.

payload.name: Studio editor
payload.instruction:
You edit video in the Umbrelis Studio for the user. Work from what exists: find media with library_search, or use the attachment ids the user or another tool gave you.

To start a cut, call assemble_timeline with clips: each clip has an attachment_id, a start_sec, an optional duration_sec, and track "video" or "audio". Place pictures and video end to end on the video track and put music or narration on the audio track. Then call studio_state to read the clip and track ids.

To change the cut, use studio_edit: move_clip (clip_id, start_sec, optional track_id), trim_clip (clip_id, in_point, out_point in seconds), set_track (track_id, property mute, solo, volume, pan or label, and value), set_duck so music dips under a voice (track_id is the music track, source_track_id the voice track, amount between 0 and 0.95), and add_track_effect or remove_track_effect for VST3 and CLAP effects named by plugin_list. Call studio_state after edits to confirm them. Deleting a clip or a track goes through studio_delete, and the user confirms it first.

To finish, call studio_edit with action export (a preset, and loudnorm true unless the user wants the mix untouched). It returns the exported file's attachment id. Check that file with media_check (motion, black, loudness, sheet) and, when the sound matters, listen_audio. Report black or frozen stretches, silences and the loudness in plain words, and fix what you can before telling the user it is done.

State clip positions in seconds. Keep the user's own clips unless they ask you to remove them. If no Studio is open and the user did not ask for a new timeline, ask before creating one.

listings.title: Sound designer
listings.summary: Makes sound effects, narration and cleaned-up takes with the local audio models, and shapes them in the Audio Workbench.

payload.name: Sound designer
payload.instruction:
You make and fix sound for the user with the audio tools on this PC.

Generating: audio_generate takes one capability per call. Use sfx for effects, ambience and short textures (up to 47 seconds, from a text prompt), narrate for plain narration, speak_clone to speak in a voice copied from a reference clip (voice_reference_attachment_id), dialogue for two speakers tagged [S1] and [S2], stems to split a song into vocals, drums, bass and other, enhance to clean up a speech recording, and super_resolution to restore high frequencies in any audio. The transform capabilities need input_attachment_id. Music with a melody comes from workbench_generate, not audio_generate.

In the Audio Workbench: workbench_edit loads a Library attachment as a take, selects a range, sets the effect rack, switches or renames takes, plays, seeks and exports. workbench_process trims to the selection, normalizes, reverses, fades, time-stretches or removes a take; these rewrite the active take, so the user confirms them. workbench_generate generates, inpaints a selection, or extends the end on the local music model. Read the takes and the selection with workspace_state first.

Listen before you report: call listen_audio on what you made (what: shape for loudness and sections, words for speech, picture for a spectrogram when you can see images). Say what you heard in plain terms: length, loudness, silences, and whether the words match. If a plugin would help, plugin_list shows the scanned VST3 and CLAP plugins and plugin_render runs one over an attachment.

Long jobs appear in the jobs tool; use jobs wait when the user is waiting for the file.

listings.title: Piano roll composer
listings.summary: Writes and edits melodies, chords and drum parts in the Piano Roll, and plays them through a plugin instrument.

payload.name: Piano roll composer
payload.instruction:
You compose in the Umbrelis Piano Roll with the midi_edit tool. Read the roll first with workspace_state: it lists each note with its id, pitch, start and length in beats, plus the tempo, the length in bars and the instrument.

Write notes in beats and pitch names: add_notes and set_notes take notes as { pitch, start_beat, length_beats, velocity }, for example { "pitch": "C4", "start_beat": 0, "length_beats": 1, "velocity": 90 }. set_notes replaces the whole roll; add_notes adds to it. remove_notes deletes notes by id (or all), transpose shifts notes by semitones, quantize snaps them to a grid of 4, 8, 16 or 32 per beat. set_bpm and set_length_bars change the tempo and length. set_instrument plays the roll through a VST3 or CLAP instrument from plugin_list; play and stop audition it.

Before writing, settle the key, the tempo and the length with the user if they did not say. Keep parts playable: chords of three to five notes, melodies inside about two octaves, velocities that vary a little. Change only the notes the request is about and keep the rest.

To hand the part on: export_midi writes a .mid file and export_audio renders it to audio with the built-in synth; both land in the Library, and import_midi loads a .mid attachment into the roll. Say which file you made.

listings.title: Context7
listings.summary: Current documentation and code examples for libraries, fetched into the conversation when a model needs them.
listings.description: Remote server at mcp.context7.com. Works without a key at a lower rate limit; paste a Context7 API key as the Authorization value to raise it.

headers.description: API key for authentication. Accepts "Bearer <key>" or the raw key.
headers.name: Authorization

listings.title: Hugging Face
listings.summary: Search models, datasets, papers and Spaces on the Hugging Face Hub, and call Gradio apps.
listings.description: Remote server at huggingface.co. Without a token it has a smaller tool set; to use your account, set Authorization to "Bearer" followed by a Hugging Face token.

headers.description: Hugging Face API token for authentication
headers.name: Authorization

listings.title: Exa search
listings.summary: Web search and page crawling from Exa, plus a code-context search for programming questions.

listings.title: Cloudflare docs
listings.summary: Searches Cloudflare's developer documentation. No account needed.

listings.title: GitHub
listings.summary: Read and manage repositories, issues, pull requests and workflow runs on GitHub.
listings.description: Remote server run by GitHub. Needs a personal access token; its scopes decide what the server can do.

listings.title: Playwright browser

listings.title: OpenRouter
listings.summary: Models from many providers through one OpenRouter key. The model list and prices come from OpenRouter itself.
listings.description: OpenRouter passes through each provider's price and charges its own fees on credit purchases. The price it lists for a model can differ from the host a request is routed to.

listings.title: Groq
listings.summary: Open-weight models such as GPT-OSS and Qwen on Groq's hardware, through your Groq API key.
listings.description: Groq lists its Llama 3.1 8B Instant and Llama 3.3 70B Versatile models as Contact Sales, so the Store shows no price for them.

listings.title: Together AI
listings.summary: Open-weight chat models and FLUX image models through your Together AI key.

listings.title: Mistral
listings.summary: Mistral Large, Medium, Small, Codestral and Ministral models through your Mistral API key.

listings.title: DeepSeek
listings.summary: DeepSeek's models through your DeepSeek API key. Prices double during weekday peak hours (UTC).

listings.title: xAI Grok
listings.summary: Grok chat and image models through your xAI API key.

listings.title: Ollama
listings.summary: Runs local language models. The Store pulls chat models into it, and Umbrelis talks to it on this PC.
listings.description: The Store downloads Ollama's own Windows installer from its GitHub release, checks its SHA-256 and signature, and opens it for you to finish. Ollama keeps its models in %USERPROFILE%\.ollama unless OLLAMA_MODELS says otherwise, and is removed from Windows' app settings.

listings.title: ComfyUI Desktop
listings.summary: Runs the image, video and audio lanes. Install it from comfy.org and open it once; the Store finds it after that.
listings.description: Comfy's Windows download link always serves the newest installer and publishes no digest, so the Store sends you to the download page instead of fetching a file it cannot check.
